companyContext: Mega Crit Games is an independent, remote game studio based in Seattle, Washington, founded by Anthony Giovannetti and Casey Yano. The studio specializes in developing design-focused strategy games in the roguelike deckbuilder genre. Their debut title, Slay the Spire (2019), became a critically acclaimed genre-defining hit, and they are currently developing and supporting its sequel, Slay the Spire 2.
brandContext: Slay the Spire 2 is the long-awaited sequel to the genre-defining roguelike deckbuilder. Set 1,000 years after the original, the Spire has reawakened, hungrier and more dangerous than ever. Featuring five playable characters (three returning, two brand new), an all-new cooperative multiplayer mode for up to four players, alternate acts, enchanted cards, and deeper strategic systems. The game launched into Steam Early Access on March 5, 2026 for Windows, macOS, and Linux.

typography.fontUses: Brand name and game title logo — a bespoke weathered medieval serif used exclusively in the Slay the Spire wordmark and marketing headlines. The typeface has a hand-hewn, ancient stone quality with slightly irregular strokes to convey dark-fantasy atmosphere.

Headings, card titles, and primary UI labels — used across the game's interface for all prominent text such as card names, section headings, menu titles, and interactive button labels. Rendered with MSDF for crisp clarity at all resolutions.

Body text, card descriptions, tooltips, and general UI copy — the default weight used for readable paragraphs, explanatory text, compendium entries, and in-game dialogue. Base size 16px, line-height 1.5 for optimal readability.
Subheadings, stat labels, and secondary emphasis — used for medium-weight annotations such as damage numbers, energy costs, keyword callouts, and navigation breadcrumbs.
Numerical data, version strings, and technical display — used for fixed-width numerical readouts, run statistics, seed codes, and debug or modding interface elements.

brandVision: Slay the Spire 2 aims to evolve the genre-defining roguelike deckbuilder by deepening strategic depth, expanding replayability through alternate acts and new systems like card enchantments and afflictions, and introducing cooperative multiplayer to create shared experiences. The game is developed through a community-driven Early Access model, with continuous iteration driven by player feedback and rigorous data-driven balancing. Mega Crit's direction is to deliver a sequel that honors the legacy of the original while boldly expanding what a roguelike deckbuilder can be.
brandValues: Community-first development: Slay the Spire's success was built on its community, and the sequel continues that ethos with Early Access transparency and direct player feedback loops. Quality over speed: Mega Crit refuses to compromise on polish—refusing to massively expand the studio or set exacting deadlines, believing that inspired work requires creative freedom. No microtransactions: The game is a complete premium product with no exploitative monetization. Design-focused innovation: Every card, relic, and system is meticulously crafted for strategic depth and meaningful player choice. Accessibility and replayability: The game is designed so no two runs are ever the same, rewarding mastery while remaining approachable to newcomers. Independent spirit: As a self-funded indie studio, Mega Crit prioritizes creative integrity and player trust above all.
